maya: Quick sync — Q1 hosted roadmap bakeoff. We have multiple customer asks (lower embedding unit cost, tighter chat tail latency, and higher rerank throughput). Need to map customer asks -> slices and call out launch criteria + biggest risks. Ideas below, pls react with thumbs and add short notes.

devon: +1. Can we make the engineering slices explicit? My brain: 1) embeddings cost (quant + caching), 2) chat latency (KV cache + kernel selection + batching policies), 3) rerank throughput & streaming optimization. Which of these are shippable in Q1?

maya: exactly. My proposal: pick two priority slices for Q1 (one cost-focused, one latency/quality). We keep rerank as early Q2 candidate unless a customer is willing to pilot dedicated capacity.

olivia: For embeddings cost slice: suggest we run a small eval on quantized embeddings (8-bit + FP16 fallback) vs baseline on our embed benchmark (search/retrieval recall). If recall drop > 0.5% we bail. Also validate downstream ranking impact.

devon: ops concern: quantization is doable but infra changes (new kernel paths) will add ~2 sprints of infra work. If we can do caching + batching improvements first, that might buy time and hit cost targets faster.

simon: SRE notes: any plan that increases burstiness (smaller batches, lower latency) will need revised autoscaling rules and a canary cadence. We need to add a capacity guardrail: reject-to-fallback when queue > 200ms. Also prefer predictable reserved slots for early pilots.

olivia: suggestion for rollout criteria (draft):
```yaml
rollout:
  canary: 10%
  metrics:
    - p95_chat_latency_ms <= 300
    - embedding_cost_per_1k <= $0.45
    - rerank_throughput_rps >= 600
    - quality_regression_pct < 0.5
  rollback_on:
    - error_rate_increase > 0.3%
    - tail_latency_spike > 20%
```

devon: +1 to those metrics. Need to be specific about how we measure "embedding_cost_per_1k" — include KV cache hit-rate in denominator? otherwise numbers misleading.

maya: Good call. Let's define cost metric as "net compute tokens + memory amortized / 1k embeddings after cache hits". I'll draft a one-pager.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline triggered: hosted-qa/quant-embed-run #342 - canary test scheduled for 2026-02-03T15:00Z

simon: For rollout policy we should include automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant (quantized vs full-precision) if p95 exceeds threshold but quality still within limits. That keeps availability.

devon: Ops trade: if we fallback to cheaper model variant frequently, customers might see inconsistent quality. Need a note in SLA and maybe an opt-in for deterministic variant.

olivia: Agree. Add an opt-in pinning flag: `model_variant=locked` that bypasses auto-fallback; reserved capacity customers get pinning by default.

maya: Action items: @devon estimate infra work (2 wks/4 wks?), @olivia produce embed eval and a small rerank eval set, @simon write canary + autoscale runbook. I'll own the one-pager and the OKR mapping.

devon: I'll estimate today, will post numbers in the doc.

olivia: I'll upload eval results by EOD Fri.

simon: I'll draft the runbook and share w/ oncall for review.

maya: Thanks — I'll update the roadmap doc and open a PR for prioritization. Link to draft: https://redwood-internal/roadmaps/q1-hosted-bakeoff (will add notes). :thumbsup:
